title: Out-of-Distribution Robust Explainer for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Post-hoc GNN explainers may highlight unreliable graph components when inference graphs contain OOD nodes and edges.

gap.claim: Post-hoc GNN explainer robustness on inference graphs containing OOD entities has received limited study.

contributions.claim: ORExplainer is a post-hoc node-level explanation framework for inference graphs containing OOD nodes.
ORExplainer uses an energy-based node-level distributional-deviation score from a pre-trained GNN and propagates it to emphasize ID nodes while suppressing OOD influence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets reportedly show that ORExplainer provides more robust explanations across diverse node-level OOD settings.
The authors report that ORExplainer outperforms existing baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for graph-structured data, motivating post-hoc explanation methods.
Existing explainers are mainly designed and evaluated when inference and training graphs are structurally or distributionally similar.
OOD nodes and edges can introduce spurious signals and cause unreliable components to be highlighted.
Robustness under OOD-contaminated inference graphs remains largely unexplored.
The paper proposes ORExplainer, describes its distributional-deviation scoring mechanism, and reports stronger robustness than existing baselines.

source_observation.claim: OOD entities can introduce spurious signals during explanation generation.

interpretation.claim: Explanation methods may need explicit mechanisms to distinguish distributionally reliable components from deployment-time anomalies.

application.claim: For graph explanation in deployment, estimate component-level distributional deviation and reduce the influence of high-deviation components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported node-level OOD settings.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the energy-based score, propagation procedure, or training objective in detail.
